people.name: Shrop Shireslasher
people.title: The soldier who chose his own orders
people.summary: A fugitive of the Stolen Sons, a breaker of doors, and the companion who kept going first—even without sight.
people.portraitAlt: Shrop’s original journal artwork: a broad cartoon figure in purple clothes, hat and scarf.
people.tokenAlt: Shrop’s yellow-bordered Roll20 token, wearing a purple hat and dark glasses.
backstory: Shrop knew his mother’s name: Caroleena, or Carolee. Much else was missing. Born to an orc father and a human mother, he had never been fully accepted by one family and never known the other. At twelve he entered the Stolen Sons. Whether he had been conscripted, sold, or taken was a question his own history could not answer.

At sixteen, he followed orders to destroy a village in the Western Vinlands after the mission was already accomplished. The raid earned him the name Shireslasher and stirred memories of his mother. He deserted the mercenaries and spent years running from them, still drawn to soldiering but determined to choose whose orders he followed.
He valued freedom while judging poverty harshly, despite his own poor childhood. Among his companions, he could insist on a funeral, let a boy win at arm wrestling and break down the next door.

progression.title: A name made in the Citadel
progression.text: Shrop helped bargain with the Hurcreles, freed Erky Timbers, recovered Shatterspike and discovered Grim in the Citadel.

progression.title: The runaway met the wider trade
progression.text: At Khundrukar, he opened doors, fought duergar and Nightscale, helped rescue commoners and found more clues about the Stolen Sons.

progression.title: A sacrifice, a curse, and Shreagle
progression.text: He sacrificed Shatterspike at Pelor’s temple. Near Ossington, Grim first transformed him into Shreagle. Thunder later restrained him when the cursed axe took hold; in Nightfang, Shrop leapt at the mooncalf while berserk.

progression.title: The candle in the Nightmare Grotto
progression.text: Shrop snuffed a candle in Crimson Crazuk’s Nightmare Grotto and released a spirit. The road north would bring the company against Pengu and a world losing its magic—the consequences of that release. The confrontation reached Frostblight, where Pengu’s fighting form collapsed into a living obsidian egg.

progression.title: A different kind of foresight
progression.text: The northern road drew him towards Grek and Frostrazor under Eldath’s guidance. He carries the Boon of Foresight, alongside Champion resilience and extraordinary strength. Those gifts sit beside his blindness; they do not erase it or explain its beginning.

progression.title: A portal took the equipment
progression.text: Xanthar persuaded Shrop and Team Biscuit to take the portal to the grotto. They arrived naked, separated from their equipment, before joining Team Gravy’s fight through the ants. The Wrinkle then trapped Gravy in Hell; Biscuit continued to Windglum. Brother Ernie recovered most of the missing gear later in the Bastion adventure.

progression.title: The front of the company
progression.text: After fighting beside Team Gravy in sunken Brindinford, Shrop returned to the Bastion. He continued going first towards the dragon whose name he had learned in the Citadel.

gifts.name: Frostmore and Foe Slasher
gifts.text: His named weapons, carried after the sacrifice of Shatterspike and his struggle with the cursed axe.

gifts.name: Storm-giant strength
gifts.text: His belt and formidable equipment turn an already imposing soldier into a force suited to impossible doors and enormous enemies.

gifts.name: Eldath’s foresight
gifts.text: Eldath’s blessing grants foresight and protection alongside his Champion endurance. He remains blind.

revisionist.title: The Stolen Sons were part of a larger market
paragraphs: Helkitrin linked the Stolen Sons to captives traded for metals from Blasingdell, Ossington and Brindinford. The mercenaries pursuing Shrop belonged to that network. Who took him from Caroleena, and what became of her, remain unknown.

revisionist.title: The axe echoed an older command
paragraphs: The cursed axe repeats a danger Shrop knew in the Vinlands: another will directing his strength. Thunder’s intervention broke that pattern on this occasion. This is a retrospective reading; Shrop is not known to have made the comparison himself.

revisionist.title: What escaped when the candle went out
paragraphs: The spirit Shrop released by extinguishing the candle was Pengu. Its freedom brought the loss of magic that followed the company into Icewind Dale, weakening Grim’s spells and Terry’s divine aid. The consequences reached beyond the north: Rigus’s magical wards failed, leaving the city open to the demon army.

Terry’s fourfold attunement and Blackrazor’s sacrifice completed the rite against Pengu. Frostblight fell and magic began to recover, while Pengu’s living obsidian egg remained. The company had fought the spirit Shrop released.

unfinished: Caroleena’s fate and the circumstances of Shrop’s conscription remain unanswered. The beginning of his blindness is not established here, and the twenty-year displacement must not be mistaken for twenty years of personal ageing.
The Bastion leaves room for the soldier’s final choice. No victory, death, cure or homecoming is written for him in advance.

traits.name: A difficult contradiction
traits.text: He values the freedom to choose his own battles, yet carries an unreasoning hatred of enemies and a harsh judgment of poverty born from his own childhood.

Hindsight: Xanthar returned those three to White Plume Mountain, where he now rules as the self-proclaimed Keraptis. They remain safely stored there and will never forgive the Brotherhood for sacrificing their sibling, Blackrazor.

people.name: Grimbledee Brightburrow
people.title: The scholar who ran out of books
people.summary: A dragon scholar compiling a great spellbook, following his ancestor Eudostis and bargaining with powers eager to use his curiosity.
people.portraitAlt: Grim’s journal portrait: a bearded gnome in green robes holding blue magical flame.
facts: Gather all known magic into one great tome
backstory: Grim’s father, Hortletott Brightburrow, sold and bound books; his mother, Deannartie, made jewelry. Uncle Theothottle Braidedbeard shared his wizard’s library and stories about dragons.

Theothottle said his grandfather Eudostis had seen a dragon while travelling with friends. A missing diamond supposedly came from its hoard, though its provenance was uncertain. Grim inherited his uncle’s burrow and spent more than thirty years exhausting the books and witnesses within reach before leaving to find a dragon himself.

His family tended his home and garden while he travelled, promising to return intact, wealthier if possible and wiser. He hoped eventually to compile all known magic in one book. Gold-eyed, carefully dressed and wildly bearded, he admitted a flaw: an ancient mystery might be worth the price of a civilization.

progression.title: Lore became a working tool
progression.text: In the Citadel, Grim scouted with his familiar, taught Terry Draconic and translated dragon lore. He urged the party to subdue the Hurcrele captives and helped return their rings.

progression.title: The dragon finally appeared
progression.text: Khundrukar brought Borol’s Ring, duergar to question, secret caches and Nightscale. Grim finally saw the dragon he had spent decades studying.

progression.title: A family face in a tomb
progression.text: At Brindinford he countered a bone devil’s summoning and carried the company safely from the bell tower with Feather Fall. Ossington brought a spirit in his mind and an elemental bargain. Nightfang then placed Eudostis’s likeness on a sarcophagus, turning the family tale into an immediate mystery.

progression.title: The past was not finished
progression.text: The Sleeper explained Eudostis’s connection to the Time Stone and Crimson Crazuk. The company returned to its eighth-level lives, then overshot its original present by twenty years. A later divine vision named twenty years without new souls while Ashardalon fed in the Bastion.

progression.title: A portal took the equipment
progression.text: Xanthar persuaded Grim and Team Biscuit to take the portal to the grotto. They arrived naked, separated from their equipment, before joining Team Gravy’s fight through the ants. The Wrinkle then trapped Gravy in Hell; Biscuit continued to Windglum. Brother Ernie recovered most of the missing gear later in the Bastion adventure.

progression.title: Knowledge before a fallen god
progression.text: Grim gathered the candle ingredients and prepared three sets of wax and wick. Terry’s fourfold attunement and Blackrazor’s sacrifice completed the Pengu ritual. Grim later approached Desayeus peacefully to ask about the Soul Totem. At level 22, he commands Spell Mastery, Signature Spells and an extensive repertoire.

gifts.name: The growing spellbook
gifts.text: He once measured his unfinished collection spell by spell. Now his repertoire reaches Wish, Time Stop, Gate and other ninth-circle workings, while the ambition of the one great tome still draws him onward.

gifts.name: Familiars and borrowed shapes
gifts.text: Queasel’s scouting and the Shreagle journeys show knowledge doing practical work: looking ahead, crossing water, and moving an entire company.

gifts.name: The ancient text
gifts.text: He keeps an ancient text holding terrible secrets, bound to the promise that it must not fall into the wrong hands. What those pages contain remains a mystery of its own.

revisionist.title: Eudostis’s captivity
paragraphs: Eudostis stole the Time Stone to free the Sleeper, inadvertently unlocking Crazuk’s prison. Lydzin later wished him into a parrot and kept him captive. The Sleeper partly repaired his mind and urged him to rest at home; his actual homecoming remains unrecorded.

revisionist.title: A scholar’s most dangerous question
paragraphs: Grim’s willingness to trade a civilization for ancient knowledge invites comparison with the route through Desayeus’s prison. He sought a fragment needed to reach Bastion; Eco died, and Findula withdrew. That comparison is interpretive. It neither supplies Grim’s private judgment nor identifies who dealt Eco’s killing blow.

revisionist.title: The book that became Brother Xanthar
paragraphs: Grim lost and eventually forgot his flesh-golem book during his dealings with the aboleth. Xanthar used it to make the body in which he appeared as Brother Xanthar.

A K-vial convinced Xanthar that he was the one true Keraptis. His power and flesh-golem body spared him the zombie fate, and he defeated the current K-clone prime to take White Plume Mountain. His equipment theft returned Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor there. Grim did not discover that destination at Ernie’s reunion.

revisionist.title: The brother Xanthar wanted Grim to remember
paragraphs: In Echoes in the Abyss, Xanthar used family warmth, dragon lore and imagined shared adventures to prepare a false memory of himself as Grim’s trusted older brother. Boss recalls the solo as an audio-led choice adventure, with memories at risk when Grim chose incorrectly.

The full backstory presents the written ordeal and both endings. The recordings, individual choices and final result have not been recovered; the plan is revealed without assigning Grim a choice he may never have made.

unfinished: The family diamond, ancient text’s contents, great spellbook’s completion and Eudostis’s safe return remain unresolved. Grim’s old notes grew more certain about his ancestor’s identity, but leave gaps in the family tree.
Ashardalon, the dragon he studied, still awaits the company in the Bastion.
Which memories did Grim surrender to Xanthar, and which voices did he recognise as false? The solo’s hidden purpose is known; its exact choices and ending still leave space for his own recollection.

people.name: Terry Stronginthearm
people.title: Faith with a hammer in its hand
people.summary: A sarcastic healer and smith, owner of Zandikar, whose fourfold attunement made the Pengu ritual possible.
people.portraitAlt: Terry’s campaign portrait: an armored dwarf holding a hammer before a golden sun.
backstory: Terry’s own account of his upbringing proceeds through goblins eaten by wolves, wolves slain by goblins, and further changes of household until he tired of the drama. A citadel at least promised three meals a day. When goblins and wolves combined to wreck that arrangement too, he took to the road and helped people—with sarcasm close at hand.

He watched over friends like newborn pups and put the tribe’s good first. Money and manners, he thought, offered little help against a hungry owlbear. He also believed the strong thrive and the weak perish, though he repeatedly healed companions who would otherwise have died.
Terry knew Shrop and Thunder through the Stolen Sons before Team Biscuit formed. His travels brought him to dwarven history, smithcraft and service as Pelor’s war priest.

progression.title: Chalk, healing and Draconic lessons
progression.text: In the Citadel he brought healing, helped unravel the twig-blight puzzle and struck a bargain with the Hurcreles. Grim’s Draconic lessons began one night at a time. Khundrukar added Gharin’s warhammer, rescued commoners, dwarven lore and Ironcore.

progression.title: A commitment made in Brindinford
progression.text: Terry committed to Pelor, helped cleanse the temple, removed mummy curses from Shrop and Grim, and used Daylight to save the Baron. Near Ossington, he found Pelor’s hidden shrine and communed with the dead paladin.

progression.title: A fortress became his responsibility
progression.text: After Imperagon’s defeat, Terry gained Zandikar and its vast smithy. The armor conveyed authority over gates and guardians while its forge drew on elemental fire.

progression.title: The north tested his independence
progression.text: Thunder saw Terry become unnaturally obedient, repeating a numerical riddle as his judgment and initiative faded. Meanwhile, the candle working made his four-item attunement valuable to Keraptis.

progression.title: The bearer the ritual needed
progression.text: Pelor’s boon let Terry attune to Wave, Whelm, Frostrazor and Blackrazor at once. The company sacrificed Blackrazor to complete the Candle of the Dark One ritual. Pengu was defeated, Frostblight fell and magic began to recover.

progression.title: A portal took the equipment
progression.text: Xanthar persuaded Terry and Team Biscuit to take the portal to the grotto. They arrived naked, separated from their equipment, before joining Team Gravy’s fight through the ants. The Wrinkle then trapped Gravy in Hell; Biscuit continued to Windglum. Brother Ernie recovered most of the missing gear later in the Bastion adventure.

progression.title: The weight of a living saint
progression.text: At the Red Keep, survivors worshipped the absent adventurers as the Blessed Company; Terry’s armor waited there. He fought through the demon army and buried Brindinford, then returned to the Bastion’s soul crisis. He is now a level-21 war cleric with one paladin level. The gods had warned of twenty years without new souls.

gifts.name: Pelor’s Boon of Attunement
gifts.text: The blessing permits four attuned magic items. It allowed Terry to complete the northern candle working that Keraptis, limited to three, could not perform.

gifts.name: The Armor of Zandikar
gifts.text: Attunement grants command of the fortress under its forge’s conditions. The six regenerating blade golems guard Zandikar; they did not travel as his companions.

gifts.name: Hammer, holy blade and healing
gifts.text: The Hammer of Thunderbolts, Holy Avenger and Ironcore stand beside the healing and intervention that repeatedly held the company together.

revisionist.title: Keraptis needed the bearer
paragraphs: The candle’s hidden requirement was attunement to all four weapons of power. Keraptis could manage three; Terry’s boon allowed four. That made the dwarf a potential target for abduction, and ultimately made him the bearer who could complete the northern working. Blackrazor was sacrificed during that rite. Its absence from the later stolen equipment records came from that earlier sacrifice.

Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor survived the working. Their later return to White Plume through Xanthar concealed another consequence of the victory: the three regarded Blackrazor as their sibling, and would never forgive the Brotherhood for giving it up.

revisionist.title: The forge was a doorway
paragraphs: Zandikar’s furnace opened onto the Elemental Plane of Fire. Its heat powered the fortress’s systems, and the armor’s command of the golem guardians depended on the forge burning.

revisionist.title: Faith could not grant every release
paragraphs: Pelor authorised passage into Desayeus’s prison while forbidding his release. Eco died, the company obtained the fragment and Findula withdrew. The difference between that permission and what followed invites a retrospective reading of Terry’s faith; his private judgment is unrecorded.

unfinished: The cause and final resolution of Terry’s altered behavior remain open. The completed Pengu ritual does not by itself establish a cure for that separate affliction.
Zandikar and the Red Keep remain distinct places. His future as priest, smith, fortress-holder or surviving companion awaits the company’s last reckoning.

traits.name: War Priest and War Caster

people.name: Thunderdrum Stringcutter
people.title: The way home, and the blood that barred it
people.summary: A performer turned thief, Brindinford guild insider, heir to a curse, and descendant of the dragon’s ancient enemy.
people.portraitAlt: Thunder’s journal portrait, a long-haired figure leaning forward with an intent expression.
backstory: Thunder’s mother was an elven musician travelling with a troupe; his human father owned a theater in Brindinford. They met during the annual festival, and Thunder was born after the performers had left town. He grew up among acrobatics, sleight of hand and drums, learning how to catch an audience before he learned how to escape one.

Curiosity eventually brought him to Brindinford to find his father. Human years had moved faster than he expected. He arrived during the old man’s final days and heard a deathbed confession: his father had been cursed as a wererat and feared passing it to his son. Thunder would not return to his mother until he could lift the inheritance. Performing sometimes gave way to burglary; a failed attempt sent him into service with the Stolen Sons, where he joined Terry and Shrop.
Thunder paid dues to Brindinford’s thieves’ guild, accessed its black markets and joined a guild takeover. Its surviving members later met him in Rigus, where their meeting ended in slaughter.

The wish to be famous sat beside the fear of going home. He collected rumors wherever he went and could smooth a room’s temper with charm, but his own family still waited without understanding his absence. The later discovery of Dydd’s blood gave his inheritance a second, much older meaning.

progression.title: Doors, traps and a difficult confession
progression.text: Thunder disarmed traps, opened locks and helped free Erky Timbers in the Citadel. He told his companions about the lycanthropy that kept him from returning to his mother.

progression.title: An entertainer became the scout
progression.text: Khundrukar brought traps, drumming, backstabs and an approach to Nightscale. In Brindinford he gathered contacts, paid his guild dues and entered its black markets. He took part in a guild takeover, scouted Pelor’s temple, survived the Wrinkle and used Saithnar’s glasses to read dragon lore for Grim and Terry.

progression.title: The hand that stopped a friend
progression.text: Near Ossington, he investigated the tarn, found the abandoned Pelorian shrine and restrained Shrop during his cursed rampage.

progression.title: The last guild meeting
progression.text: Thunder arranged a meeting in Rigus with the last members of the Brindinford thieves’ guild. They were slaughtered there. He obtained blood-spattered notes telling of the guild’s earlier losses, the Baron’s secret fight over adamantum, the drow and Varachus’s Acheron obligation. The killers at the meeting are not named in the recovered account.

progression.title: Underworld rumours in Rigus
progression.text: Guild rumours told Thunder of a healthy-looking child born lifeless, depleted Mercykiller ranks and a missing fifth founder of Rigus’s ruling Brotherhood. The source guild is unidentified.

progression.title: The captaincy with a price
progression.text: The Ethereal Anchor opened passage to the Deliverance and bound Thunder’s soul to it. Pepper warned that dying while wearing the pendant would make him the ship’s captive captain. The northern vision showed the ship searching for him; the condition still held.

progression.title: A portal took the equipment
progression.text: Xanthar persuaded Thunder and Team Biscuit to take the portal to the grotto. They arrived naked, separated from their equipment, before joining Team Gravy’s fight through the ants. The Wrinkle then trapped Gravy in Hell; Biscuit continued to Windglum. Brother Ernie recovered most of the missing gear later in the Bastion adventure.

progression.title: Dydd’s words in his own voice
progression.text: Thunder received the Soul Totem fragment and spoke Dydd’s invocation in Desayeus’s prison. He has gained controlled lycanthropy, the master thief’s talents and the Boon of Swiftest Bladework. The journey now brings Dydd’s descendant towards Ashardalon, without prewriting the confrontation.

gifts.name: Controlled lycanthropy
gifts.text: He can take rat and hybrid forms, though prolonged use carries a warning of eroding control. That progression sits beside the older family account of a curse he once had never outwardly manifested.

gifts.name: The Ethereal Anchor
gifts.text: The pendant opens portals, binds him to the Deliverance and focuses his Swiftest Bladework boon. Dying while wearing it would make him replace Pepper as captive captain.

gifts.name: Planar Rapier and Pale Piercer
gifts.text: Named blades carried by a thief whose great strengths also include observation, investigation and moving through places others cannot reach.

revisionist.title: The rumour about a child with no soul
paragraphs: The guild reported Cierith Bloodwyn’s firstborn as healthy-looking but lifeless. Later revelations connect the soul famine to Ashardalon’s feeding. Thunder heard the rumour before its cause was established; the missing fifth founder remains a separate mystery.

revisionist.title: The hunted blood was a weapon in someone else’s plan
paragraphs: Dydd’s blood made Thunder useful against the dragon whose original heart she wounded. Aameul sent the Cathezar after him to help obtain Ammet, the demon serving as Ashardalon’s heart, for his own struggle against Hethradiah.

revisionist.title: Pepper’s freedom could become Thunder’s prison
paragraphs: Thunder was warned that death while wearing the pendant would bind his soul aboard the Deliverance and release Pepper to the afterlife. That consequence remains unfulfilled.

revisionist.title: Two inheritances, neither chosen
paragraphs: The wererat curse kept Thunder from his mother; his descent from Dydd drew him towards Ashardalon. Their effect on his wish to choose his own future is a retrospective interpretation, with no new claim about either bloodline’s origin.

unfinished: His mother’s reunion, the final state of his curse, and the Deliverance’s ultimate captaincy remain open. Neither Pepper’s release nor Thunder’s death is assumed.
He has spoken the invocation, but no recorded final confrontation yet shows what he chose to do with it before Ashardalon.

memories.caption: An earlier portrait of Thunder, performer and scout.

statistics.intro: The latest available full character record is dated 1 September 2026. The Bastion battle figures below record conditions during that encounter.
statistics.leveling: The epic record preserves Thief Rogue 23 and 623,440 XP. Individual level-up dates are not recorded. The Sleeper episode returned the company to its own eighth-level selves: a flashback, not lost advancement.
statistics.awardsNote: Personal adventure awards, not cumulative character XP. The last entry combines the Brindinford and Ossington completion awards with the recorded early Nightfang deeds; these awards are not added again to the XP total above.

journalSnapshot.intro: The recorded Bastion battle, with its equipment, blessings and battle conditions.

inventory.name: Gloves of Dexterous Thievery and Locksmith’s Bane
inventory.text: Distinctive tools of the trade beside his ordinary thieves’ tools and disguise kit.

inventory.name: Pendant of the Ethereal Anchor
inventory.text: The key to the Deliverance, the focus of his swiftest-bladework boon, and the bearer of Pepper’s very particular warning.

inventory.name: Planar Rapier, Pale Piercer and MoonTouched Dagger
inventory.text: Named blades in the same collection as a Shortbow +3 and an unusually varied supply of magical arrows.

inventory.name: Shirt of the Fire Snake
inventory.text: The personal clothing project already appears among his Citadel-era achievements. The later sheet still carries the shirt.

inventory.name: Cloak of Arachnida and Ring of Invisibility
inventory.text: Magic for climbing and concealment, among his scouting equipment.

inventory.name: Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location
inventory.text: A protective amulet carried during the pursuit of Dydd’s descendant.

inventory.name: Portable Hole
inventory.text: Magical storage alongside his bow, drum and lockpicks.

inventory.name: Clockwork Faefly and Clockwork Inkbeetle
inventory.text: Small crafted curios sharing his pack with a Monocle of Clarity and Wand of Secrets.

inventory.name: Dragon, Unicorn and Owlbear Snugglebeasts
inventory.text: Three soft keepsakes listed on his sheet.

inventory.name: Drum and Disguise Kit
inventory.text: The performer’s tools remain part of the rogue, beside the acrobatics and sleight of hand learned with his mother’s troupe.

traits.name: A performer’s way with people
traits.text: He defuses tension, gathers rumors and spreads gossip. Creativity guides him; fame remains a personal ambition.

traits.name: The inherited rat
traits.text: Keen Hearing and Smell, Natural Armor and Controlled Lycanthropy belong to his recorded inheritance. The transformation carries a warning against remaining in animal forms too long.

traits.name: The master thief’s precision
traits.text: The sheet records 10d6 Sneak Attack, Reliable Talent, Fast Hands and Use Magic Device.

traits.name: Survival by inches
traits.text: Uncanny Dodge, Evasion, Elusive, Defensive Duelist and Stroke of Luck describe a very different defense from Shrop’s armor.

traits.name: Swiftest Bladework
traits.text: His boon is tied to wearing the Ethereal Anchor. The sheet’s Dexterity 27 belongs to a gifted and equipped incarnation, not an unmodified starting score.

traits.name: Languages and signs
traits.text: Common, Draconic, Elvish, Orc and Undercommon, plus the coded speech and signs of Thieves’ Cant.

people.inventoryNote: Xanthar’s portal left Team Biscuit naked and separated from its equipment. Ernie later recovered most belongings; Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor were still missing. Hindsight: Xanthar returned those three to White Plume Mountain, where he now rules as the self-proclaimed Keraptis. They remain safely stored there and will never forgive the Brotherhood for sacrificing their sibling, Blackrazor.

people.name: Brunn Ironbelly
people.title: An old soldier’s spark
people.summary: A dwarf chasing buried steel found a living infestation—and a second company fighting for the same way out.
people.portraitAlt: Brunn’s original circular token: a roaring red-bearded dwarf with an axe.
people.tokenAlt: Brunn Ironbelly’s original Roll20 portrait token.
backstory: Brunn had been drinking in the Blasingdale tavern since morning, trading stories for ale and ignoring the flinches his laughter caused. His coin was gone, his armor smelled of smoke and his axe was well acquainted with an anvil.

He had come south following rumours of dwarven steel and its makers’ ghosts in a fortress buried beneath Brindinford. When the other wanderers spoke of fungus and fortune, he slammed down his mug. If it paid, he was in.

progression.title: A different company took the boat
progression.text: Brunn joined Rook, Nox and Elira aboard the Deliverance. Xanthar sent them to map the underground stronghold and return within his deadline.

progression.title: Steel met the living ruin
progression.text: His hunt for buried weapons led into spores, animated bodies and old traps. A planar gate was feeding the stronghold’s corruption.

progression.title: Eight companions against the colony
progression.text: After the falling boat and the Deliverance’s rescue, Brunn reached sunken Brindinford. Team Gravy joined Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder against the giant ants.

progression.title: The trap beyond the ants
progression.text: The Wrinkle’s portal trap caught Brunn and the other three members of Team Gravy. It had been set for Team Biscuit. They remain lost in Hell to this day, while Team Biscuit continued to Windglum and the Bastion adventure.

gifts.name: The repaired axe
gifts.text: His battered axe had been repaired repeatedly, and his armor smelled of smoke.

gifts.name: The Berserker’s calling
gifts.text: He follows the Path of the Berserker, still willing to fight despite his empty purse.

revisionist.title: The old ruin had a celestial deadline
paragraphs: Devas in hobgoblin shapes were trying to stop the planar infestation. A ward barred them from the gate; Hayyel had prepared to destroy the complex if the gate remained open. Mortal explorers could enter where the celestials could not.

revisionist.title: Fortune became company
paragraphs: Brunn joined for payment and ended up fighting beside seven other adventurers in the ant-held city. Reading that as a growing attachment to the company is interpretive. No new oath or change in his mercenary motives is established.

revisionist.title: The trap was meant for the other company
paragraphs: The Wrinkle’s portal trap was set for Team Biscuit. It caught Team Gravy instead and sent all four to Hell, where they remain. No escape or homecoming has been recorded.

unfinished: Brunn remains lost in Hell with Rook, Nox and Elira, caught in the Wrinkle’s portal trap after the ant battles. What dwarven relics he kept and what became of his search remain unanswered; his return has not been told.

inventory.name: The much-repaired axe
inventory.text: His biography’s weapon has seen more repair work than most anvils. No enchantment or attack bonus is recorded for it.

inventory.name: Smoke-scented armor
inventory.text: Battered armor from his years of soldiering.

inventory.name: The tavern mug
inventory.text: The mug slammed down in Blasingdale belongs to his introduction: stories for ale, and a willingness to join if the venture paid.

traits.name: Berserker and old soldier
traits.text: A Mountain Dwarf following the Path of the Berserker, with a laugh that makes the tavern flinch.

traits.name: Practical appetite
traits.text: He seeks payment, buried dwarven steel and the makers’ ghosts. Whether the ruin yielded a particular relic remains unknown.

traits.name: An unspent spark
traits.text: Broke and weathered, he still joins the expedition with enthusiasm.

people.name: Rook Kestrel
people.title: The hunter beneath the sky
people.summary: He followed a blight down from the peaks and found himself in tunnels, a falling boat, and the company of rather desperate goblins.
people.portraitAlt: Rook’s original circular token: a brown-feathered aarakocra archer.
people.tokenAlt: Rook Kestrel’s original Roll20 portrait token.
facts: The blight, downriver from the high peaks
backstory: Rook’s arrival drew a crowd in Blasingdale. Few locals had seen an aarakocra; after the novelty faded, he became a curiosity by the tavern window, wings tucked against the cold. He had followed the same spreading blight that troubled Elira, tracing it downriver from the high peaks.

Now his money and arrows were running low. He watched for anyone who might hold a weapon—or pay for one. Brunn’s laugh ruffled his feathers; Nox’s smile made him look away. The sky already felt distant before the expedition carried him beneath the earth.

progression.title: Following the sickness into stone
progression.text: Rook followed the blight into a stronghold where fungus and water carried sickness. The river hunt continued through narrow underground passages.

progression.title: Everyone suddenly admired his wings
progression.text: When the escape boat appeared in empty air above Brindinford Falls, the goblins clung to Rook in hope of being saved. Then the Deliverance appeared alongside the falling craft, its spectral crew ready to secure a most unconventional arrival.

progression.title: The hunt became a street war
progression.text: In sunken Brindinford, Rook fought with both companies against an organised ant colony holding the ruined streets and tunnels.

progression.title: The trap beyond the ants
progression.text: The Wrinkle’s portal trap caught Rook and the other three members of Team Gravy. It had been set for Team Biscuit. They remain lost in Hell to this day, while Team Biscuit continued to Windglum and the Bastion adventure.

gifts.name: Bow and dwindling arrows
gifts.text: An archer’s eye and a dwindling quiver came down from the peaks with him. In the grotto, every narrow passage brought the hunt closer.

gifts.name: Wings in a confined world
gifts.text: The goblins clung to his wings when the boat fell above Brindinford Falls. The tunnels and buried streets offered much less room for flight.

revisionist.title: The ants were being directed
paragraphs: A neogi master, a queen and the bell-tower apparatus directed the colony through filaments and foreign devices. Whether the companies reached or destroyed that system remains unrecorded.

revisionist.title: The trail kept taking away the horizon
paragraphs: Rook’s path from the high peaks runs through a tavern window, tunnels and a brief fall into open air. His wings sharpen that contrast in a retrospective reading; no private fear of confinement is established.

revisionist.title: The trap was meant for the other company
paragraphs: The Wrinkle’s portal trap was set for Team Biscuit. It caught Team Gravy instead and sent all four to Hell, where they remain. No escape or homecoming has been recorded.

unfinished: Rook is still lost in Hell with the other three members of Team Gravy. His return to the peaks, the fate of the blight he hunted, and any later ranks or achievements remain unwritten.

inventory.name: Bow and dwindling arrows
inventory.text: His original token shows the archer; his biography says the arrows and coin were running low.

inventory.name: Wings held close
inventory.text: The goblins clung to his wings above the falls. His aarakocra wings are part of his body.

traits.name: Hunter on the blight’s trail
traits.text: An Aarakocra Ranger of the Hunter path, following the sickness downriver from the high peaks.

traits.name: A watchful eye
traits.text: He scans the tavern for someone who can hold a weapon or pay for one, even after local curiosity about him has faded.

traits.name: Small frictions in the company
traits.text: Brunn’s loud laugh ruffles his feathers; Nox’s returning smile makes him look away. Both details belong to his own introduction.

people.name: Nox Veyra
people.title: An insult to the pact
people.summary: A seeker of dangerous sigils found a realm that refused her familiar—and took the refusal personally.
people.portraitAlt: Nox’s original yellow-bordered token: a dark-haired tiefling with red horns.
people.tokenAlt: Nox Veyra’s original Roll20 portrait token.
facts: Old magic beneath the strange river
backstory: Nox arrived with the last caravan before the passes froze, her purse light and patience thinner. She called herself a scholar of sigils, while flames curled at her fingertips. Horns, brimstone and her smile kept villagers at a distance as she listened for rumours of old magic.
The grotto’s corruption tore her fiendish familiar apart before it could manifest. She called it an insult. Without its extra eyes and ears, she pressed on towards the old magic deeper in the ruin.

progression.title: A scholar joined the expedition
progression.text: The Deliverance carried Nox, Brunn, Rook and Elira towards the river cut. Her search for lore continued under Xanthar’s mapping task and return deadline.

progression.title: The familiar could not follow
progression.text: Her familiar could not manifest in the fungal realm. The planar gate continued feeding the corruption even where corridors could be cleared.

progression.title: The company grew in the dark
progression.text: The escape led to sunken Brindinford. Nox fought alongside Team Biscuit and her own company to keep the ants from closing their route.

progression.title: The trap beyond the ants
progression.text: The Wrinkle’s portal trap caught Nox and the other three members of Team Gravy. It had been set for Team Biscuit. They remain lost in Hell to this day, while Team Biscuit continued to Windglum and the Bastion adventure.

gifts.name: Pact and fire
gifts.text: Her pact grants fire and a fiendish familiar. Its patron remains unnamed.

gifts.name: The scholar of sigils
gifts.text: Dangerous old marks are her chosen field. Rumors of buried magic gave the scholar a reason to venture where the river ran strange.

revisionist.title: The boundary rejected other spirits too
paragraphs: The corruption rejected extraplanar spirits, including fiends, fey and familiars. Both Nox’s fiendish companion and Elira’s fey spirit failed at that boundary.

revisionist.title: The apparent hobgoblins had their own constraints
paragraphs: The disguised devas were trying to stop the gate, but its forbiddance barred them. Mortal explorers could enter. Their presence establishes no bargain with Nox’s patron or alliance between fiend and angel.

revisionist.title: The trap was meant for the other company
paragraphs: The Wrinkle’s portal trap was set for Team Biscuit. It caught Team Gravy instead and sent all four to Hell, where they remain. No escape or homecoming has been recorded.

unfinished: Nox remains lost in Hell with Brunn, Rook and Elira. Her patron’s identity, the restoration of her familiar, and any lasting claim upon the grotto’s magic remain unanswered; no escape from the trap has been recorded.

inventory.name: Dangerous sigils
inventory.text: Her chosen field of study and the lure that drew her towards the strange river. No named grimoire is supplied by the biography.

inventory.name: The absent familiar
inventory.text: Her pact companion could not manifest in the grotto. Without it, she lost the extra eyes and ears she expected.

traits.name: The Fiend and the Chain
traits.text: Boss’s roster names the Fiend patron path; her own biography calls her a chain-warlock. The specific patron remains unnamed.

traits.name: Fire at the fingertips
traits.text: Small curls of flame betray the more combustible side of the scholar of sigils.

traits.name: Pride under pressure
traits.text: She treats the grotto’s rejection of her familiar as an insult and a challenge, sharpening her desire to claim its old magic.

people.name: Elira Moss-Weaver
people.title: Following the wound
people.summary: The moss witch followed dreams of a black river into the grotto, where its corruption prevented her fey companion from forming.
people.portraitAlt: Elira’s original circular token: a wood elf druid in green with a wooden staff.
people.tokenAlt: Elira Moss-Weaver’s original Roll20 portrait token.
facts: Dreams of black water and broken stone
backstory: Elira followed the rot before she saw the river’s strange glow. Dreams of black water winding through broken stone had drawn her towards Blasingdale, and the journey only deepened her unease. She stood at the edges of rooms, listened, and sketched unfamiliar fungi in a worn journal while the locals muttered moss witch.

A little fey companion should have moved beside her, shaped from leaf-whispers and roots. Beneath Brindinford, the fungal influence unraveled that magic before the spirit could form. She could still feel its absence. Determined to find the wound poisoning the land, she continued into the corridors without the companionship her own magic should have offered.

progression.title: Dreams found their river
progression.text: Elira followed her dream’s warning aboard the Deliverance. Brunn, Rook and Nox accompanied her towards the growth covering the underground stronghold.

progression.title: The sickness had a doorway
progression.text: A planar gate fed the grotto’s growth. Necromantic spores animated bodies within it.

progression.title: No longer walking alone
progression.text: Team Gravy escaped to sunken Brindinford and joined Team Biscuit against the ants. Elira’s hunt for the source of the sickness continued through the ruined town.

progression.title: The trap beyond the ants
progression.text: The Wrinkle’s portal trap caught Elira and the other three members of Team Gravy. It had been set for Team Biscuit. They remain lost in Hell to this day, while Team Biscuit continued to Windglum and the Bastion adventure.

gifts.name: The worn field journal
gifts.text: She sketches unfamiliar fungi in its worn pages while listening from the edges of rooms.

gifts.name: Underdark and fey magic
gifts.text: Her Circle of the Land follows the Underdark. The grotto’s corruption still prevented her fey companion from forming.

revisionist.title: Cleansing could have meant annihilation
paragraphs: Hayyel planned to destroy the complex with its flammable stockpile if the planar gate could not be stopped. That alternative would burn the place Elira hoped to heal.

revisionist.title: Who sent the dreams?
paragraphs: Elira’s dreams of black water and broken stone led towards the grotto. They may be read as a summons, but the sender is unidentified: no deity, patron or other intelligence has been established.

revisionist.title: The trap was meant for the other company
paragraphs: The Wrinkle’s portal trap was set for Team Biscuit. It caught Team Gravy instead and sent all four to Hell, where they remain. No escape or homecoming has been recorded.

unfinished: Elira remains lost in Hell with Team Gravy. The source of her dreams, the fate of her fey companion, and the land’s final recovery remain open; neither her return nor the destruction of the grotto’s gate is supplied by the tale.

inventory.name: The worn fungus journal
inventory.text: Her biography records sketches of unfamiliar fungi in this field journal. No magical properties are identified.

inventory.name: Wooden staff
inventory.text: Visible in her original portrait token, carried by the green-clad druid.

inventory.name: The missing fey companion
inventory.text: A little spirit of leaves and roots should have walked beside her; the corruption breaks its manifestation before it can form.

traits.name: A druid of the Underdark
traits.text: A Wood Elf of the Circle of the Land (Underdark), drawn to a wound beneath the surface.

traits.name: Quiet attention
traits.text: She stays at the edges of rooms, listens, and records the small signs others dismiss.

traits.name: Dreams and determination
traits.text: Black water and broken stone lead her towards Blasingdale. She continues even without the companionship her magic should provide.
